questions.q_en: Which of the following statements about light is incorrect?
options_en: Light exhibits both wave and particle nature.
Light can travel in a vacuum.
Light can propagate in a curved path naturally.
The speed of light is approximately 3  X  10^8 m/s.
questions.solution_en:
• Light always propagates in a straight line unless it undergoes refraction or reflection.

• Light is a form of energy that enables vision by entering our eyes, allowing humans and creatures to see objects.

• Light is an electromagnetic wave exhibiting both wave-like (e.g., diffraction) and particle-like (e.g., photon) properties

• Light travels at a constant speed of approximately 3 x 108 1m/s in a vacuum (or air).

questions.q_en: Why can't we see an object in complete darkness?
options_en: Because light is absorbed by objects in the dark
Because no light is emitted or reflected towards our eyes
Because our eyes are not adapted to darkness
Because objects do not exist in darkness
questions.solution_en:
• Vision is possible only when light emitted or reflected by an object reaches our eyes.

• The human eye acts like a camera, using its parts to capture and process light to form an image that the brain interprets.

• Light forms an inverted, real image on the retina.

• The brain receives these impulses, inverts the upside-down image, and interprets it as an upright visual perception, enabling us to "see" the object.

questions.q_en: Which of the following is a non-luminous object?
questions.solution_en:
• A non-luminous object does not produce its own light but reflects light from other sources. The moon is visible due to reflected sunlight.

• Translucent materials allow partial passage of light, such as paraffin wax. Glass and water are transparent, while rubber is opaque.

• Opaque objects either reflect or absorb light; they do not allow light to pass through them.

questions.q_en: Which of the following is not a law of reflection?
options_en: The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.
The incident ray, the reflected ray, and the normal all lie in the same plane.
The angle of incidence is always 90°.
The laws of reflection hold for both smooth and rough surfaces.
questions.solution_en:
• The angle of incidence can vary; it is not always 90°.

• Laws of Reflection

○ The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.

○ The incident ray, the reflected ray, and the normal to the surface at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.

○ Reflection is the turning back of light into the same medium after striking a surface (e.g., opaque materials like mirrors).

questions.q_en: Which of the following is a use of concave mirrors?
questions.solution_en:
• Concave mirrors are used as shaving mirrors because they provide a magnified image when the object is within the focal length.

• Uses of Concave Mirrors

○ Torches, Searchlights, and Headlights: Produces powerful parallel beams by reflecting light from the focal point.

○ Shaving Mirror: Forms a magnified, upright image when the face is between the pole and focal point.

○ Dentist's Mirror: Creates a large, virtual image of teeth for close examination when held near the object.

○ Solar Furnaces: Concentrates sunlight to a focal point to generate intense heat for melting or cooking.

questions.q_en: Which phenomenon causes the twinkling of stars?
questions.solution_en:
• Atmospheric refraction causes the twinkling of stars due to continuous bending of light.

• As the path of rays of light coming from the star goes on varying slightly, the apparent position of the star fluctuates and the amount of starlight entering the eye flickers - the star sometimes appears brighter, and at some other time, fainter, which is the twinkling effect (Source NCERT)

questions.q_en: Total internal reflection occurs when:
options_en: Light moves from rarer to denser medium
Light moves from denser to rarer medium with incidence angle greater than critical angle
Light moves at any angle from denser to rarer medium
questions.solution_en:
• When the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle, total internal reflection occurs.

• When light travels from an optically denser medium to a rarer medium at the interface, it is partly reflected back into the same medium and partly refracted to the second medium. This reflection is called the internal reflection (Source NCERT)

• The violet light bends the most while the red light bends the least because of the difference in their wavelengths

questions.q_en: A rainbow formation is caused due to:
options_en: A combination of refraction, reflection, and dispersion
questions.solution_en:
• A rainbow forms due to refraction, dispersion, and reflection inside raindrops.

• A rainbow is always formed in a direction opposite to that of the Sun.

• The water droplets act like small prisms.

• They refract and disperse the incident sunlight, then reflect it internally, and finally refract it again when it comes out of the raindrop.

• Due to the dispersion of light and internal reflection, different colours reach the observer's eye

• Reflection is a phenomenon in which there is turning back of light into the same medium after striking a surface.

• The splitting of white light into its seven constituent colours (VIBGYOR) when passing through a prism due to varying wavelengths is called Dispersion.

• The redirection of light in various directions by small particles in the atmosphere, causing phenomena like the blue sky is called scattering

questions.q_en: A plane mirror forms an image that is 15 cm behind it. If the mirror is moved 5 cm toward the object, what is the new image distance from the object?
questions.solution_en:
• Initially, object-to-image distance = 15 cm (behind mirror) + 15 cm (object in front) = 30 cm.

• Mirror moves 5 cm closer, reducing object distance to 10 cm; image remains 10 cm behind, total distance = 20 cm.

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements regarding refraction of light. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(a) When light travels from a denser to a rarer medium, it bends away from the normal.

(b) The refractive index of a medium is the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to the speed of light in that medium.

(c) If the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle, light passes into the rarer medium with maximum speed.
questions.solution_en:
• Laws of Refraction:

○ "The incident ray, the refracted ray and the normal to the interface of two transparent media at the point of incidence, all lie in the same plane."

○ "The ratio of sine of angle of incidence to the sine of angle of refraction is a constant, for the light of a given colour and for the given pair of media. This law is also known as Snell's law of refraction.

• Statement (c) is incorrect because when the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle, total internal reflection occurs, and light does not pass into the rarer medium.

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements regarding the power of a lens. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(a) The power of a convex lens is positive, while that of a concave lens is negative.

(b) The power of a lens is measured in diopters.

(c) The power of a lens is given by P = f (in meters).
questions.solution_en:
• The power of a lens is a measure of its ability to bend light. It depends on how strongly the lens converges (brings together) or diverges (spreads apart) light rays.

• The power of a convex lens is positive.

• The power of a concave lens is negative.

• The power of a lens is measured in a unit called the diopter, abbreviated as "D."

• One diopter is defined as the power of a lens with a focal length of 1 meter.

• Power of Lens = 1/f
